channel.title: NPR Topics: Education
channel.description: We've been to school. We know how education works. Right? In fact, many aspects of learning — in homes, at schools, at work and elsewhere — are evolving rapidly, along with our understanding of learning. Join us as we explore how learning happens.

item.title: Special education head at Education Department abruptly resigns
item.description: The leader of the Education Department's special education office told employees she is resigning after less than four months in the role and as the agency overall is morphing and shrinking.

item.title: Federal civil rights data about students is finally out. It's different under Trump
item.description: The Education Department gathers a massive tranche of civil rights data about public school students. It's now available but harder to parse than in the past.

item.title: Wesleyan president calls Trump's tax-exempt proposal 'extraordinary overreach'
item.description: The Trump administration wants to end tax-exempt status for universities with certain race-based programs. Wesleyan President Michael Roth says the plan could frighten schools.

item.title: Trump administration pushes to remove tax exemption for private colleges with DEI policies
item.description: The Trump administration is proposing a rule that would strip private schools and colleges of their tax-exempt status if they provide targeted help to students based on their race.

item.title: As millions of kids lose SNAP food benefits, free school meals are also at risk
item.description: Food stamps have a direct link to other critical resources, such as free breakfast and lunch at school. Now, experts say they're starting to see that link break.

item.title: Understanding the tech giants' oversized influence in American schools
item.description: Big tech companies like Apple and Microsoft use devices, training and conferences for teachers and students to embed in schools. The New York Times' Natasha Singer discusses the impact in Coding Kids.

item.title: How Dolly Parton's literacy work affected Indigenous communities in Australia
item.description: In Australia, the queen of country music, Dolly Parton, is being remembered for her work in advancing children's literacy, particularly in Indigenous communities.
